messages:
pagerbot: [INCIDENT] High-rate 401s detected from prod-auth-proxy -> suspicious vector. Severity: P2. Link: https://redwood.inc/alerts/6098765432 :rotating_light:

alice.k: seeing repeated 401s from a handful of internal IPs + a couple of S3 access logs that contain Authorization header fragments. flagging for triage. short sample: 
```
GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.internal
Authorization: Bearer sk-***-a1b2c3
```

devon.r: @alice.k can you confirm the logs are from prod S3 and not staging? any customer IDs or PII in the samples?

alice.k: confirmed prod bucket "redwood-prod-auth-logs"; sample shows truncated token only (no email/ids). still considered sensitive. added a note to the incident channel doc.

security-oncall: taking lead. immediate actions: 1) rotate service account tokens that can be used with auth-proxy 2) set temporary denylist for the observed IPs 3) enable more aggressive logging mask for auth headers 4) start scan for other buckets with similar patterns. tagging legal if we find PII.

ops-bot: Runbook: https://runbooks.internal/incidents/auth-leak - recommended play: token-rotate -> scrub & preserve copies -> customer-impact-assess. Suggested commands: 
```
# rotate svc token
aws iam create-access-key --user-name svc-auth-proxy
# update k8s secret
kubectl set secret deployment/auth-proxy -n prod --from-literal=TOKEN=<new>
```

anita.m: i'm on pager. will do rotation and coordinate with platform to push new secret. @mike.t can you prep the rollback/fallback model in case of failures? :thumbsup:

mike.t: prepping canary rollback and a fallback to read-only tokens. PR for k8s secret update: https://git.redwood/p/1234 - will test staged rollout in 3m.

alice.k: found two other S3 keys with similar stdout patterns (redwood-prod-batch-logs). marking them for scan. starting a limited copy-and-scrub to preserve evidence (read-only snapshot).

devon.r: any customer-facing impact yet? requests failing? metrics show a 0.4% spike in failed requests for a specific customer org (org-472). alerting CSM.

security-oncall: no confirmed exfil yet. treat as potential leakage. prioritize token rotation and log scrub. capture timeline: first 401s 6098765405, sample log arrive 6098765418.

anita.m: rotated svc token for auth-proxy (svc-auth-proxy). Verified new secret in k8s and auth-proxy picked it up. Commands executed and checked health endpoints.

mike.t: canary rollout succeeded. traffic looks normal on canary nodes; latency unchanged. fallback path tested (read-only tokens) and healthy.

ops-bot: Actions completed checklist: [rotate_tokens: done] [denylist_ips: applied] [scrub_started: in-progress] [preserve_evidence: done] [legal_notify: pending if PII found]

alice.k: scrub job found 3 log files with full Authorization header prior to rotation window. moving to secure archive and redacting. created ticket: https://triage.redwood/t/3345

devon.r: CSM notified for org-472. Customer impact: some requests retried, small increase in latency during rotation window. No data loss reported.

security-oncall: next steps: 1) complete S3 scrub and secure archive 2) rotate any related service tokens (scheduler, batch workers) 3) run a bucket-wide grep for "Authorization:" strings 4) prep a short incident note for customers if we escalate.

mike.t: rotated batch-worker keys (svc-batch-worker). Verified job runs for last 2 cycles.

anita.m: handing off to security-oncall for follow-up and postmortem. I'm going offline in 15m but will ping if anything fails. :white_check_mark:

security-oncall: acknowledged handoff. will run full scan, coordinate legal if PII, and draft customer-facing blurb if needed. postmortem ETA: EOD.

pagerbot: Incident status updated to RESOLVED-MITIGATED at 6098765460 by security-oncall. Summary: rotated implicated tokens, scrubbed exposed logs, applied denylist, no confirmed customer data exfiltration. Postmortem required.

alice.k: adding remediation items to backlog: stricter logger filters, pre-rotate hooks, and alert for raw auth header writes.

devon.r: thanks all. great quick work.

mike.t: dropping the deployment runbook notes and commands in the incident doc.

security-oncall: closing channel for live ops. will reopen if new evidence appears.
